subject: tech
title: Electricity and Batteries
about: Electricity is the energy that makes things light up, move and make sound; it comes from the wall outlet (sent from a power plant far away) or from a battery that stores it, and a charger fills the tablet's battery back up (K2-CS-02, the parts that make a device work). Electricity is a bridge topic, since NC science teaches it in Grade 4, so this level stays simple and calm: what needs power, plus and minus ends, solar panels, and the safety rules. Read it together, and say the safety rules in your own words too.
tip: Walk around the house and sort things together: this needs electricity, this does not, and only grown-ups plug things in.

cards.q: Lights, fans and tablets all need a kind of energy to work. What is it?
cards.note: Electricity is energy that makes things light up, move or make sound.

cards.q: Electricity flows into a lamp. What does the lamp do?
cards.note: Light, sound and movement: electricity can make all three.

cards.q: Electricity flows into a fan. What does the fan do?
cards.note: A motor inside the fan turns electricity into spinning.

cards.q: The lamp plugs into the wall. Where does that electricity come from?
cards.note: Wires carry electricity from a power plant along tall poles and into the walls of your house.

cards.q: A flashlight has no cord. Where does it get electricity?
cards.note: A battery stores electricity so a thing can work with no cord.

cards.q: Which one needs electricity to work?
cards.note: A tablet, a lamp and a fridge need electricity. A book and a ball do not.

cards.q: Which one works with no electricity at all?
cards.note: Lots of fun things need no power: balls, books, crayons, blocks.

cards.q: The tablet battery is empty. What fills it up again?
cards.note: The charger pours electricity from the wall into the battery. A grown-up plugs it in.

cards.q: The battery is all the way empty. What does the tablet do?
cards.note: No electricity, no tablet. Charge it and it wakes up again.

cards.q: A battery has two ends with marks on them. What are the marks?
cards.note: Look for the + and − marks. The battery only works when each end goes the right way.

cards.q: A battery goes into a toy backwards. What happens?
cards.note: Match plus to plus and minus to minus. A backwards battery gives no power.

cards.q: What may go into a wall outlet?
cards.note: Never put fingers or anything else in an outlet. Only a plug goes in, and only a grown-up puts it there.

cards.q: Who plugs things into the wall?
cards.note: Plugs are a grown-up job. Ask, and a grown-up will plug the charger in for you.

cards.q: Water and electricity must stay far apart. Where do you keep the tablet?
cards.note: Keep drinks, sinks, tubs and pools away from anything that plugs in.

cards.q: Your hands are wet from the sink. What do you do before touching the tablet?
cards.note: Dry hands first. Water and electricity do not mix.

cards.q: You find a tiny round battery on the floor. What do you do?
cards.note: Batteries are not toys and never go in your mouth. Small ones are extra dangerous, so hand it to a grown-up right away.

cards.q: A solar panel sits in the sun. What does it make?
cards.note: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity. Some calculators and houses use them.
A battery is like a little tank full of electricity, ready for when you need it.
